LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 RESPONSIVE LISTENING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Responsive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Responsive Listening, part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to actively respond to what is being said?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or offline for techniques for listening responsively. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted,

2. team up with others to listen to an audio recording, television or radio programmes,

3. practise showing empathy

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or offline for techniques for listening responsively. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted digital devices, assistive technology or be assisted,
2. team up with others to listen to an audio recording, television or radio programmes,
3. practise showing empathy

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Responsive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy as the learner nurtures leadership skills as they practise showing empathy when listening to another person.

Values:
Peace is promoted as learner displays tolerance as they team up with others to listen to an audio recording, television or

radio programmes.
